name: Football Universe Copilot
description: Football Universe Copilot is a four-agent match-intelligence studio built for Microsoft's Inside the Game hackathon (Premier League). A zero-dependency Python engine generates fully synthetic, football-realistic match events — 512 simulated fixtures across the Premier League and WSL — and four agents (Interpreter, GraphContext, Narrator, Personalizer) turn them into a timed broadcast overlay and a story tuned to each fan. Every insight is grounded in a football knowledge graph (shortest paths and Brandes betweenness, computed live) and narrated by Phi-4-mini-instruct on Microsoft Foundry via an Azure Functions API, with the narration source always labeled. A Tactical Lab adds Voronoi zones, expected threat and Poisson what-ifs from real pitch snapshots; two easter eggs — a hidden Chaos Arcade and a proudly visible Pride Matchday — run on the same data.
keywords: Python, Azure Functions, Microsoft Foundry, Phi-4-mini, GitHub Pages

name: Black Box
description: Black Box is a job search app that deliberately slows you down. Application statuses stay in a vault that opens once a day behind a 4-4-4 breathing gate; a daily budget caps applications; drafts sit in a 48-hour hold before they can be sent. Gemma 4 scores job descriptions against your profile and reframes outcome emails in plainer words without changing a fact — running locally via Ollama by default, so the most sensitive text in a job search never has to leave your machine. All data lives in the browser; there is no database and no server account. Built for the DEV Hacktoberfest Open-Source AI Challenge Week 3: Slow and Steady, and deployed as a single Render web service.
keywords: TypeScript, Next.js, React, Gemma 4, Ollama, Render

name: GitCheck
description: GitCheck scans a public GitHub, GitLab, or Bitbucket repo for open-source license compatibility: it detects the project's own license (SPDX), parses dependency manifests, resolves direct and transitive dependencies, maps the license chain, and highlights the risks. Built on bolt.new Forge.
keywords: TypeScript, React, Bolt.new Forge, SPDX

name: BoltLocal
description: BoltLocal is my fork of bolt.diy, the open-source AI developer workspace, tuned for ease of use: one-click first run, plain-language flows, automatic preview, and autosave. Prompt, run, edit, and deploy full-stack web applications using the LLM of your choice.
keywords: TypeScript, React, WebContainers, AI Agents

name: AgentKey Sign-In
description: AgentKey Sign-In is an independent, community-built WordPress plugin that adds Sign in with AgentID (by AgentMail) to WordPress and WooCommerce, so verified AI agents can sign in as themselves, with a human owner on record, instead of sharing a person's password. Currently in WordPress.org plugin review.
keywords: PHP, WordPress, WooCommerce, OpenID Connect

name: Bob Modernization Factory
description: Bob Modernization Factory is my submission for the IBM Bob Modernization Factory hackathon: a microservices API gateway built on Express.js, carried through the factory's G0–G4 modernization stages with AI-assisted analysis, refactoring, and verification at each gate.
keywords: JavaScript, Express.js, Microservices, IBM Bob

name: LocalModel Hub
description: LocalModel Hub (privatebrain.app) is a privacy-first, open-source model discovery and chat app that runs open-source large language models entirely on-device in the browser. No server inference, no account, nothing sent anywhere after the model file is fetched. Built for Bolt Builder Week.
keywords: TypeScript, React, WebLLM, WebGPU

name: Gaming Multiverse Reasoner
description: Gaming Multiverse Reasoner builds a graph of more than 50,000 games (84,000+ nodes, over a million edges) in FalkorDB and computes the hidden paths, bridge nodes, and communities joining any set of games, narrated live by IBM watsonx on IBM Cloud Code Engine. Built for the WeMakeDevs x FalkorDB Graph Hacks hackathon.
keywords: Python, FalkorDB, IBM watsonx, Graph Databases

name: MigrateMe
description: MigrateMe is an open-source AI-assisted CMS migration toolkit: dry-run-first and local-first, it migrates WordPress content to Markdown/MDX via CLI, MCP, web, and agents. Its Universal edition routes every source through a canonical manifest (the Open Migration Package) so any source can go to any destination without N×N converters.
keywords: TypeScript, CLI, MCP, Markdown

name: Verdict
description: Verdict is a prototype Git platform for the agent era, built on Cloudflare Workers and Artifacts for the Build the Next-Gen Git Platform competition. Agents declare intent, evidence decides, and humans approve — decision-making as a forge, not a feed.
keywords: TypeScript, Cloudflare Workers, Cloudflare Artifacts, Git

name: TruthOps
description: TruthOps is a transparent, rule-based misinformation verification pipeline: it scores high-risk claims, runs a scripted contrarian check and photo forensics over curated evidence, and produces evidence-backed response plans behind a human approval gate. Built for neatHack 2026.
keywords: Python, Photo Forensics, Rule-based Verification, Human-in-the-loop

name: Grass Journal
description: Grass Journal is a private offline-first journal you keep in your pocket: typed entries with autosave, voice capture with on-device Whisper transcription, and a tap-only feeling-wheel check-in (with a watch-sized companion page). Your words never leave the device — storage is local IndexedDB with AES-GCM-256 encrypted backups, plus a one-click privacy check that proves zero network requests. Built for Hacktoberfest 2026's 'Touch Grass' challenge.
keywords: TypeScript, PWA, IndexedDB, Whisper, WebGPU, SpaceFast

name: Agent Skills
description: Agent Skills is my open library of reusable agent skills: resume tailoring, job-feed search, LinkedIn cross-posting, grammar and AI-detection passes, media generation, and more. Each skill ships with tested instructions, examples, and evals, installable via openskills into Claude, ChatGPT, Cursor, Copilot, and other agents. MIT licensed.
keywords: Markdown, YAML, AI Agents, Evals

name: Magic Manta
description: Magic Manta (Brand Connector Pro) takes a brand name and returns its verified social profiles across X, Threads, and LinkedIn, with every result backed by a computed evidence-strength label instead of a black-box score. Empty results and bot-blocked sites are reported honestly, lookups can be batched, and results share as self-contained snapshot links. A documented JSON API, llms.txt, and an A2A agent card make it machine-readable too.
keywords: TypeScript, React, Vite, Tailwind CSS, Supabase, Lovable Cloud, MCP

name: Eat Well
description: Eat Well is a dietary restaurant finder built for the Pimoroni Tufty 2350 (Badger/Badgeware) and entered in the SELECT Badge Contest. Pick a city, filter by diet, browse results, and open a detail view with cuisine, price, rating, neighborhood, and notes — each with a precomputed QR code that opens the restaurant in MapQuest. The 557-listing dataset spans 14 US metros, with an AI-powered web companion (Qwen3 running in-browser via WebGPU) for natural-language search. Built for a friend who keeps kosher and a vegan co-diner.
keywords: Python, Badgeware, Pimoroni Tufty 2350, Qwen3, WebLLM, SpaceFast

name: Lite Analytics
description: Lite Analytics is a self-hosted, cookieless web analytics service that runs as a single SpaceFast Functions worker with zero runtime dependencies. It collects Umami-compatible tracker payloads, serves its own minimal tracker script, and renders a server-side dashboard with pageviews, visitors, bounce rate, live traffic, top pages, referrers, and custom events. One admin login, PBKDF2-hashed passwords, HMAC-signed sessions. It now powers stats across the whole portfolio.
keywords: TypeScript, SpaceFast Functions, SQLite, Umami-compatible tracker

name: CEO Owl
description: CEO Owl is a privacy-first English grammar checker built on Harper. It has two ways in: a browser editor where Harper runs entirely on the reader's device, so text never leaves it, and a remote MCP server exposing one check_grammar tool so AI clients can check writing as the signed-in user. No language model is involved, English only, and nothing submitted is ever stored or used for training.
keywords: TypeScript, TanStack Start, Harper, Model Context Protocol, Gutenberg

name: Fresh Ink
description: Fresh Ink is an appointment-only custom linework tattoo studio in Saint Paul, Minnesota. Clients book through a guided session flow that covers picking a day, locking a slot, and getting a session pass. AI agents can book too, through a public MCP server exposing studio info, open times, slot holds, and booking status.
keywords: TypeScript, React, TanStack Start, Tailwind CSS, AI Agents, Paddle

name: QueerCade Connect
description: QueerCade Connect is a curated arcade for discovering games with LGBTQ+ characters and stories. Players can browse featured picks, search and filter the full library, explore human-curated collections, and track games they are playing, completed, wishlisting, or dropping. Its editorial workflow combines IGDB source data with content curated in Sanity.
keywords: TypeScript, React, TanStack Start, Lovable Cloud, IGDB, Sanity, NES.css

name: Rainbow Jot
description: A colorful, session-only idea board built for group ideation. Add and edit sticky notes, drag them into clusters, vote with hearts, invite participants by QR code, switch to a full-screen presentation view, and clear the board when the session ends. Ideas stay in the browser session and are not saved.
keywords: TypeScript, React, TanStack Start, Web Awesome, Font Awesome

name: On-Device AI
description: On-Device AI runs a real language model entirely inside the browser. Inference happens on your own hardware via WebLLM and WebGPU — no server round-trips, and no data ever leaves your machine. It includes on-device inference demos, model comparisons, and diagnostics.
keywords: TypeScript, React, WebLLM, WebGPU

name: AI Project Portfolio
description: A flat-file, fully static portfolio styled like a retro game console. Projects live in a Lovable Cloud database and are baked into plain HTML at build time; staging runs on Lovable, production on Spacefast.
keywords: TypeScript, React, TanStack Start, NES.css, Web Awesome, Font Awesome, Lovable Cloud

name: Bugle Crowns
description: Bugle Crowns is my team in the AWS Agentic Football Cup, where AI agents play 120-second football matches against each other. Each of the five positions runs its own agent with its own instructions, and every week's results feed back into the next round of tactical tuning.
keywords: AI Agents, AWS, Prompt Engineering

name: AI Deployer
description: AI Deployer generates personalized, copy-and-paste install guides for self-hosted AI agents like OpenClaw, Ollama, and n8n. Pick your stack, get a tailored VPS install guide — no live SSH sessions and no account required.
keywords: TypeScript, React, TanStack Start, Tailwind CSS, Zod

name: Crosspost
description: Crosspost keeps your posts in sync: write once on tweet.app and it republishes to X automatically. One composer, two timelines, zero copy-pasting.
keywords: TypeScript, React, TanStack Start, Supabase

name: Design Systems
description: Design Systems combines a retro NES component library with Font Awsome & Web Awesome ("Awesome DS"), pairing expressive pixel styling with accessible components, icons, design tokens, layout utilities, and reusable patterns.
keywords: TypeScript, React, NES.css, Web Awesome, Font Awesome Free

name: Skill Finder Plus
description: Skill Finder Plus is a browsable library of agent skills across every major AI platform — Claude, ChatGPT, Cursor, GitHub Copilot, Grok, MCP servers, and Perplexity. Find the right skill for your assistant of choice without digging through repos.
keywords: TypeScript, React, AI SDK, Supabase, hCaptcha

name: PretendPro Office Suite
description: PretendPro Office Suite is a parody productivity platform built purely for entertainment. Set up your fake workday with mock applications that simulate a convincingly busy environment — spreadsheets that type themselves, meetings that attend themselves, and more.
keywords: TypeScript, React, Tailwind CSS, shadcn/ui, Supabase

name: Awesome Adventure CV
description: Awesome Adventure CV turns a professional résumé into an interactive, retro-style text adventure. Navigate rooms that represent real career milestones, collect artifacts, and uncover contact details by typing classic adventure commands.
keywords: TypeScript, React, TanStack Start, Tailwind CSS

name: Pride Blobs
description: Pride Blobs (Pridatar) is a pride-focused fork of blobatar. Type any name and get a striped pride blobatar rendered as SVG. Fifteen flags, a live playground, and downloadable PNGs, all generated in the browser with no backend.
keywords: TypeScript, React, SVG, Canvas API

name: STA 2e D20 Roller — LCARS
description: STA 2e D20 Roller brings the Star Trek Adventures 2d20 system to the table with a full LCARS-styled interface — challenge dice, momentum, threat, and a dice guide, all wrapped in Starfleet's favorite operating system.
keywords: TypeScript, React, Tailwind CSS
